    Engines and scale

    Source: vignettes/articles/engines-and-scale.Rmd
    engines-and-scale.Rmd

    This guide is the English version of Motores y escala. lupa writes its messages and tables in Spanish, so the output below, including the tables this page builds from the package, is in Spanish.

    This page is the reference of perfilar_dbi() and plan_perfilado_dbi() for whoever is going to profile a database in production:

    • what is computed in the engine and what is brought into R;
    • how much work each option asks for;
    • what is declared;
    • what is not estimated.

    The walkthrough with an example is in Profiling a database. The help ships with the package: ?perfilar_dbi, ?plan_perfilado_dbi and ?requisitos_motor. It is the complete source for each argument and each returned field.

    The examples run against SQLite and DuckDB in memory every time the page is built. What needs another engine is described without running it and with its source.

    Default values

    The table comes from the signatures of the 2 functions when this page is built. A dash means that the function does not have that argument. For the arguments that choose between options, the one that applies by default is shown and, in parentheses, the others.

    argumento perfilar_dbi() plan_perfilado_dbi()
    universo "tabla_completa" ("muestra_motor") "tabla_completa" ("muestra_motor")
    muestra_motor NULL NULL
    muestra Inf Inf
    orden_muestra NULL NULL
    metricas c("validos", "distintos", "moda", "basicos", "mediana", "desvio") c("validos", "distintos", "moda", "basicos", "mediana", "desvio")
    estrategia_distintos "exacta" "exacta"
    estrategia_mediana "exacta" ("aproximada_motor") "exacta" ("aproximada_motor")
    politica_costo "todas" ("por_cardinalidad") "todas" ("por_cardinalidad")
    bloque_muestra "con_muestra" ("solo_agregados") "con_muestra" ("solo_agregados")
    max_consultas Inf Inf
    dialecto "auto" "auto"
    incluir_valores TRUE TRUE
    tamano_lote NULL NULL
    tamano_lote_planos 20L 20L
    tamano_lote_distintos 2L 2L
    instrumentar TRUE FALSE
    umbral_cardinalidad 0.5 0.5
    avisar_costo_distintos TRUE —
    umbral_segundos_aviso_distintos 30 —
    avisar_costo_moda TRUE —
    umbral_segundos_aviso_moda 30 —
    avisar_costo_mediana TRUE —
    umbral_segundos_aviso_mediana 30 —
    avisar_derrame_estimado TRUE —
    umbral_bytes_aviso_derrame_estimado 0 —
    max_celdas_muestra 1.000.000 1.000.000
    max_bytes_muestra 536.870.912 (512 MiB) 536.870.912 (512 MiB)
    bloque_filas NULL NULL
    max_bytes_procesamiento 536.870.912 (512 MiB) 536.870.912 (512 MiB)
    max_bytes_materializacion 536.870.912 (512 MiB) 536.870.912 (512 MiB)
    columnas_opcionales character(0) —
    aplicabilidad NULL —
    sentinelas_numericos c(-9, -99, -999, -9999, 999) —

    Consequences for a run in production:

    • With universo = "tabla_completa" (universe = whole table) and muestra = Inf (sample), the SQL aggregates go through the whole table. With those same values, the block perfil_muestra (sample profile) tries to bring into R all the rows that max_celdas_muestra and max_bytes_muestra allow. muestra bounds only that read, never the aggregates. To bound the work of the engine there is universo = "muestra_motor" (engine sample); to bring no rows, bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados" (sample block = aggregates only).

    • instrumentar (instrument) is TRUE in perfilar_dbi() and FALSE in the plan: the run times each query and the plan does not.

    • perfil_muestra is computed with perfilar() on the rows brought in, with muestra = Inf and no caps of its own. The caps were already applied when reading. That is why the discovery of patterns, types and dates goes through all those rows. perfilar() in memory, instead, does it by default on a sample of 100,000 rows. The other arguments of perfilar() arrive through ....

      In universo = "muestra_motor", the materialization is bounded before dbFetch(n) with a conservative bound on the maximum row size. Long texts are requested as length and summary: that way their content cannot make the fetch exceed that bound. A type without a safe bound is probed one row at a time. The part that fits is kept if the budget runs out. A cut, a short final sample or a query failure leaves metadata and emits lupa_aviso_muestra_motor.

    What is computed in the engine and what is brought into R

    perfilar_dbi() returns an object of class perfil_dbi with 2 blocks. They come from different universes and do not replace each other:

    • resumen_tabla (table summary): SQL aggregates that the engine computes (counts, completeness, cardinality, mode, extremes, mean, median, standard deviation). It carries one row per column and metric in resumen_tabla$sql.
    • perfil_muestra: the full profile of perfilar() on the rows brought into R, with its findings and its coverage of diagnostics.

    What goes into each block is decided by 4 arguments:

    argument decides
    universo on which rows the engine computes the aggregates: the whole table ("tabla_completa") or a selection made by the engine itself ("muestra_motor", with muestra_motor = n required)
    muestra how many rows are brought into R for perfil_muestra; Inf brings all the ones the caps allow
    orden_muestra (sample order) which rows are brought and whether the read is reproducible
    bloque_muestra whether any row is brought ("con_muestra", with sample) or only the aggregates are computed ("solo_agregados")

    The usual combinations:

    configuration SQL aggregates (resumen_tabla) rows brought into R (perfil_muestra)
    default the whole table all the ones max_celdas_muestra and max_bytes_muestra allow
    muestra = n the whole table up to n: the first ones the engine returns, or the first ones by orden_muestra
    universo = "muestra_motor", muestra_motor = n up to n rows selected by the engine the rows actually materialized, cut by muestra and the caps
    bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados" whatever universo says none: perfil_muestra is NULL and the coverage says no_solicitado (not requested)

    bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados" is independent of universo. With muestra_motor, the aggregates still use the selection of the engine, but no rows are selected, read or kept in the client:

    • meta$materializacion$estado says no_solicitado;
    • meta$bloques$filas_vistas is 0.

    The example uses a table of 2,000 rows in SQLite in memory.

    con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:")
set.seed(11)
n <- 2000
tramites <- data.frame(
  id_tramite = seq_len(n),
  categoria = sample(c("A", "B", "C", "D"), n, replace = TRUE),
  monto = round(stats::rlnorm(n, 9, 1.1), 2),
  edad = c(sample(18:85, n - 20, replace = TRUE), rep(NA, 20))
)
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "tramites", tramites)
    por_omision <- perfilar_dbi(con, "tramites")
con_muestra <- perfilar_dbi(con, "tramites", muestra = 500, orden_muestra = "id_tramite")
del_motor <- perfilar_dbi(con, "tramites", universo = "muestra_motor", muestra_motor = 300)
solo_agregados <- perfilar_dbi(con, "tramites", bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados")

alcance <- function(x) {
  r <- x$resumen_tabla
  data.frame(
    universo = r$meta$universo,
    n_resumen = r$columnas$n[r$columnas$columna == "id_tramite"],
    validos_resumen = r$columnas$n_validos[r$columnas$columna == "id_tramite"],
    filas_en_r = if (is.null(x$perfil_muestra)) 0 else n_filas(x$perfil_muestra)
  )
}
rbind(
  por_omision = alcance(por_omision),
  con_muestra = alcance(con_muestra),
  del_motor = alcance(del_motor),
  solo_agregados = alcance(solo_agregados)
)
#>                      universo n_resumen validos_resumen filas_en_r
#> por_omision    tabla_completa      2000            2000       2000
#> con_muestra    tabla_completa      2000            2000        500
#> del_motor       muestra_motor      2000             300        300
#> solo_agregados tabla_completa      2000            2000          0

    The metric n always keeps the total of the table, also with muestra_motor. The other SQL metrics of that universe are observations of the selection of the engine, not extrapolations to the universe.

    resumen_tabla$columnas carries 15 fields per column; perfil_muestra, the full profile of perfilar(), carries 117. The accessors hallazgos(), columnas(), cobertura(), n_filas() and sql_perfil() work on both kinds of object. Their contract is in Leer un perfil (Reading a profile, in Spanish).

    Without a sample, the protection of personal data, if requested, cannot classify the columns. It then protects the cell values of all of them: mode, extremes, mean, median and standard deviation stay omitido_por_privacidad (omitted for privacy).

    con_proteccion <- perfilar_dbi(
  con, "tramites", bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados",
  proteger_datos_personales = TRUE
)
table(sql_perfil(con_proteccion)$estado)
#> 
#>              calculado              no_aplica omitido_por_privacidad 
#>                     34                      7                     19
table(sql_perfil(solo_agregados)$estado)
#> 
#> calculado no_aplica 
#>        51         9

    With a sample, the classification is done on perfil_muestra and also reaches the summary. The detail of what is masked is in Alcance y cobertura (Scope and coverage, in Spanish).

    Sampling metadata: 2 paths

    There are 2 places with sampling metadata, and they describe different things:

    path exists when describes
    perfil_muestra$meta$origen_dbi$muestreo the block of rows was requested and read (bloque_muestra = "con_muestra"), with any universo the read into R: filas_solicitadas, filas_obtenidas, acotado_en, metodo, reproducible and the statement sql_muestra
    resumen_tabla$meta$muestreo only with universo = "muestra_motor" the selection of the engine: metodo_muestreo, sesgo_muestreo, tamano_muestra, fraccion, universo and the identifiers of the local copy

    In the usual case —tabla_completa with muestra— the second path is NULL. A script that reads it out of habit, without checking for NULL, computes on nothing:

    is.null(con_muestra$resumen_tabla$meta$muestreo)
#> [1] TRUE
lectura <- con_muestra$perfil_muestra$meta$origen_dbi$muestreo
str(lectura[c("filas_solicitadas", "filas_obtenidas", "acotado_en", "metodo",
              "reproducible")])
#> List of 5
#>  $ filas_solicitadas: num 500
#>  $ filas_obtenidas  : num 500
#>  $ acotado_en       : chr "motor"
#>  $ metodo           : chr "primeras_filas_segun_orden"
#>  $ reproducible     : logi TRUE

    With muestra_motor both paths show up, and their sizes answer different questions:

    • filas_obtenidas, from the read into R: how many rows perfilar() received;
    • tamano_muestra, from the selection of the engine: how many the engine query asked for.
    seleccion <- del_motor$resumen_tabla$meta$muestreo
str(seleccion[c("metodo_muestreo", "sesgo_muestreo", "tamano_muestra",
                "fraccion", "universo", "filas_obtenidas")])
#> List of 6
#>  $ metodo_muestreo: chr "random_limit"
#>  $ sesgo_muestreo : chr "por_fila"
#>  $ tamano_muestra : num 300
#>  $ fraccion       : num 0.15
#>  $ universo       : num 2000
#>  $ filas_obtenidas: num 300

    In resumen_tabla$meta$muestreo:

    • tamano_muestra: the effective size requested from the query;
    • filas_solicitadas: the original request;
    • filas_pedidas: the request after the caps;
    • filas_obtenidas: the rows that the local copy returned.

    If muestra is smaller than muestra_motor, meta$materializacion$n_filas can exceed n_filas(perfil_muestra).

    The cardinality of a sample is published with status observado_muestra (observed in the sample). It is what was seen in the sample, with the universe next to it. It does not estimate the one of the universe without a declared estimator.

    Without orden_muestra, the rows brought are the first ones the engine returns, in an order that SQL does not guarantee. reproducible says so. With orden_muestra, the read is declared reproducible only if the combination of columns is unique in the whole table. The package checks it (orden_unico_verificado).

    Sampling forms in the engine

    With universo = "muestra_motor", the selection is made by the engine with the first form that its dialect offers and its probe accepts. The order is fixed in the code:

    order form offered to size obtained
    1 TABLESAMPLE RESERVOIR (n ROWS) DuckDB exactly n rows
    2 TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM (p) PostgreSQL, SQL Server whole blocks: it varies around the request and can give 0 rows in a small table
    3 TABLESAMPLE BERNOULLI (p) (in DuckDB, (p PERCENT): there a bare number is a row count) PostgreSQL, DuckDB row by row: it varies little around the request, at the price of going through the table
    4 TABLESAMPLE (p PERCENT) SQL Server by pages
    5 SAMPLE (p) Oracle row by row
    6 pseudorandom order with the limit of the dialect any engine with a limit exactly n, at the price of sorting the whole table

    The fixed-quantity form goes first because 2 queries of the same profile must see samples of comparable size. The block forms cost less on large tables, and that is why they come before the row-by-row ones. But their size jumps. DuckDB lets it be seen on the same table of 5,000 rows, asking for 20% with 6 seeds:

    duck <- suppressMessages(DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb()))
DBI::dbWriteTable(duck, "t", data.frame(id = seq_len(5000)))
contar <- function(muestreo, semillas = 1:6) {
  vapply(semillas, function(s) {
    sql <- paste("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t TABLESAMPLE", sprintf(muestreo, s))
    DBI::dbGetQuery(duck, sql)[[1]]
  }, numeric(1))
}
tamanos <- rbind(
  bloques = contar("20 PERCENT (system, %d)"),
  fila_por_fila = contar("20 PERCENT (bernoulli, %d)"),
  cantidad_fija = contar("RESERVOIR (1000 ROWS) REPEATABLE (%d)")
)
colnames(tamanos) <- paste0("semilla_", 1:6)
tamanos
#>               semilla_1 semilla_2 semilla_3 semilla_4 semilla_5 semilla_6
#> bloques            2048         0         0      5000      2048         0
#> fila_por_fila      1025       996       984       963       960       985
#> cantidad_fija      1000      1000      1000      1000      1000      1000

    Out of 1,000 rows requested:

    • block sampling gave between 0 and 5,000;
    • row-by-row sampling, between 960 and 1,025;
    • fixed-quantity sampling, always 1,000.

    What each form implies is published:

    • TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM publishes sesgo_muestreo = "por_bloques" (sampling bias = by blocks) with the reason sesgo_muestreo:tablesample_system_por_bloques. If it receives 0 rows or less than half of the requested ones, a broader form is tried once. The methods, the retry and the rows obtained stay in resumen_tabla$meta$muestreo. If the retry reaches the request, no warning is emitted. Only the short final sample stays no_disponible (not available) with muestra_inestable:tablesample_system_tamano_insuficiente and emits the degradation warning.

    • The pseudorandom order publishes sesgo_muestreo = "por_fila" (by row). In SQL Server, where the function is NEWID(), the median under muestra_motor only accepts that form if:

      • the table has up to 100,000 rows;
      • the requested sample is at least 20% of the table;
      • the projection, of 650 ms per million rows per pending median, does not go over 1,000 ms.

      They are constants of the code, not measurements of the run. Outside those limits, the median stays no_disponible with capacidad_no_aceptada:newid_costo_excede_presupuesto.

    • If no form is accepted, the SQL metrics stay no_disponible. They are never replaced by results of the whole table.

    • If the sample comes back empty, the metrics with scope muestra are published as NA with status no_disponible and a reason muestra_vacia:.... Zero is not published, and the column is not concluded to be empty.

    Caps on the read into R

    perfil_muestra has 2 caps, which do not touch any aggregate query:

    • max_celdas_muestra (1,000,000 cells by default) is resolved before reading, with the row count and the width of the schema.
    • max_bytes_muestra (512 MiB by default) is crossed with the budget of the spool. In the engines that allow it, it uses the catalog. In the others, it starts with a small block and adapts dbFetch(n). The sample is not brought in whole to be cut in R. Measured in PostgreSQL 16 and SQL Server (benchmark/medir_tope_muestra.R, run of 2026-11-10): 200 rows with a text of a million characters and a 250 KB binary (250 MB) reach the spool in 27 to 28 KB, each long value as its length and its MD5; with max_bytes_muestra = 1e6 on 2,000 texts of 8,992 characters, 109 rows are read, 0.99 MB, and meta$materializacion$tope_que_mando is "bytes". The CSV, in benchmark/datos/, keeps the date, the environment and the fingerprint of the code.

    If muestra = n and a cap is stricter, the smaller one rules. The coverage of diagnostics of perfil_muestra declares the cells or bytes observed, the threshold and which cap ruled. Inf in a cap turns it off. With a cap of 1,000 cells on 4 columns:

    acotado <- perfilar_dbi(con, "tramites", max_celdas_muestra = 1000)
str(acotado$perfil_muestra$meta$origen_dbi$muestreo[c(
  "filas_solicitadas", "filas_maximas_por_celdas", "celdas_solicitadas",
  "filas_obtenidas", "acotado_en"
)])
#> List of 5
#>  $ filas_solicitadas       : num Inf
#>  $ filas_maximas_por_celdas: num 250
#>  $ celdas_solicitadas      : num 8000
#>  $ filas_obtenidas         : num 250
#>  $ acotado_en              : chr "motor"
"muestra_perfilado" %in% cobertura(acotado$perfil_muestra)$diagnostico
#> [1] TRUE

    plan_perfilado_dbi() anticipates the cut of cells in attr(plan, "tope_muestra") and warns that the one of bytes will need the probe.

    The work is governed by 4 other limits:

    argument what it bounds when it runs out
    max_consultas number of queries of the run the remaining metrics stay no_disponible and the coverage says presupuesto_agotado (budget exhausted)
    max_bytes_materializacion bytes of the local copy of muestra_motor, bounded before each dbFetch(n) and checked before each write spool_presupuesto_excedido and muestra_inestable:presupuesto_materializacion; the part that fit is kept
    max_bytes_procesamiento state retained by the read in blocks and by the reread of the local copy if the object exceeds the limit, the sample is discarded with lupa_aviso_muestra_motor and tope_que_mando = "procesamiento" is published
    bloque_filas turns on the pass through the whole table in blocks of that size —

    bloque_filas = n (row block) computes in R the summary of the whole table, without retaining all the rows. It reads the table in blocks of n rows from a single result set (dbSendQuery() and dbFetch(n)). The coverage is read in meta$bloques$filas_vistas. perfil_muestra is still the diagnostic sample bounded by muestra and the caps. The drivers without proven incremental retention —DuckDB among them— stay no_disponible with their reason and a warning lupa_aviso_muestra_motor.

    por_bloques <- perfilar_dbi(con, "tramites", bloque_filas = 500, muestra = 100)
por_bloques$resumen_tabla$meta$bloques$filas_vistas
#> [1] 2000
n_filas(por_bloques$perfil_muestra)
#> [1] 100

    Caps on the approximate comparison

    The caps of detectar_duplicados_aproximados() (detect approximate duplicates) and of the vocabulary diagnostic cut work in R. They do not cut the queries that an engine already ran. This example recreates the table of suppliers of Escala y duplicados (Scale and approximate duplicates, in Spanish) so that each output is independent.

    The length of the values

    A normalized distance loses its power to tell values apart when the texts are long. The measure of the detector is Jaro-Winkler with p = 0.1. It shows with 2 texts that differ in exactly 100 characters, at different lengths.

    distancia_cien_cambios <- function(largo, semilla) {
  set.seed(semilla)
  texto <- sample(letters, largo, replace = TRUE)
  otro <- texto
  cambios <- sample(largo, 100)
  otro[cambios] <- ifelse(otro[cambios] == "a", "b", "a")
  stringdist::stringdist(
    paste(texto, collapse = ""), paste(otro, collapse = ""),
    method = "jw", p = 0.1
  )
}
largos <- c(500, 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000)
data.frame(
  largo = largos,
  distancia = vapply(largos, function(largo) {
    round(median(vapply(1:5, distancia_cien_cambios, numeric(1), largo = largo)), 3)
  }, numeric(1))
)
#>   largo distancia
#> 1   500     0.162
#> 2  1000     0.142
#> 3  2000     0.074
#> 4  4000     0.047
#> 5  8000     0.027

    The 100 differences are the same: what changes is how much they weigh in the text. Past a certain length, the distance drops below the threshold of 0.10. Then 2 texts that differ in 100 characters count as almost equal.

    That is why the detector does not compare values longer than max_largo_valor (maximum value length; 10,000 characters by default, an assumption of the code). The cap does not remove the effect, it bounds it: a column of long texts can ask for a smaller one. It is measured on the string that is really compared, with the columns already joined and normalized. If it is exceeded, the whole combination stays out of scope and is declared. With a cap of 20 characters, the string of supplier and line of business does not fit:

    corto <- detectar_duplicados_aproximados(
  proveedores, columnas = c("proveedor", "rubro"), max_largo_valor = 20
)
corto$alcance[, c(
  "max_largo_valor", "largo_maximo", "columnas_excluidas_largo", "n_pares_hallados"
)]
#>   max_largo_valor largo_maximo columnas_excluidas_largo n_pares_hallados
#> 1              20           31         proveedor, rubro               NA

    largo_maximo is the length of the compared string, not the one of each column. n_pares_hallados is NA, not zero: nothing was compared. With max_largo_valor = Inf there is no cap and no length is measured: that field is NA, not zero.

    The vocabulary diagnostic of perfilar() has its own cap, max_largo_valor_vocabulario, which is not inherited. The one of the detector is passed with perfilar(duplicados_aproximados = list(max_largo_valor = ...)). In perfilar(), the same cap also declares the coverage of the costly text operations that are not run on those values.

    The vocabulary work in perfilar()

    perfilar() looks for nearly identical variants within each text column (casi_duplicados_vocabulario, near-duplicate vocabulary), comparing their distinct values in pairs. Comparing 2 values of lengths L1 and L2 costs on the order of L1 × L2. That is why the budget, max_trabajo_vocabulario, is measured in character comparisons: 2e10 by default. When it falls short, it compares the first forms in alphabetical order —not a sample— and declares the rest. With a minimal budget it shows:

    recorte <- cobertura(ajustado)
recorte <- recorte[recorte$diagnostico == "proximidad_vocabulario", ]
writeLines(strwrap(paste0(recorte$columna, ": ", recorte$motivo), 88))
#> proveedor: El vocabulario excede el alcance de comparación: se evaluaron 7 de 7 valores
#> distintos, que son 5 formas normalizadas, y se comparó entre sí a las 4 primeras en
#> orden alfabético. Eso son 6 de 10 pares posibles y 1.531 de 2.555 comparaciones de
#> caracter. Quedaron 1 forma y 4 pares sin comparar por max_trabajo. 1 grupo de formas
#> cercanas no se formó porque sus frecuencias fueron parecidas: el criterio de variante
#> rara no pudo distinguir una forma correcta de otra. Se identificó 1 par cercano con
#> asimetría <= 2.0.

    The alphabetical order makes the result independent of the order of the rows of the file. The search for dependencies has its own budget: max_trabajo_dependencias, of 1e8 row-pair comparisons by default. Inf turns off either of the 2.

    How many pairs are returned

    max_resultados (100 by default) does not decide what is compared, but how many pairs are returned: it keeps the closest ones. With a cut of 2, on the 3 pairs at distance 0:

    dos <- detectar_duplicados_aproximados(
  proveedores, columnas = c("proveedor", "rubro"), max_resultados = 2
)
dos$pares[, c("fila_1", "fila_2", "distancia", "tipo_par")]
#>   fila_1 fila_2 distancia           tipo_par
#> 1      3      4         0             exacto
#> 2      1      2         0 exacto_normalizado
dos$alcance[, c("truncado", "distancia_corte", "corte_en_empate")]
#>   truncado distancia_corte corte_en_empate
#> 1     TRUE               0            TRUE

    corte_en_empate = TRUE (cut in a tie) warns that at least one pair as close as the kept ones was left out. It is not truncado (truncated) under another name: if the cut falls on a unique distance, it is FALSE even if something was cut. To bring all the tied ones, max_resultados has to go up.

    Among tied pairs, the tie-break uses the content of the values and not the position of the rows. Reordering the table does not change which pairs stay:

    ids_conservados <- function(datos, resultado) {
  a <- datos$id[resultado$pares$fila_1]
  b <- datos$id[resultado$pares$fila_2]
  sort(paste(pmin(a, b), pmax(a, b), sep = "-"))
}
invertidos <- proveedores[8:1, ]
dos_invertidos <- detectar_duplicados_aproximados(
  invertidos, columnas = c("proveedor", "rubro"), max_resultados = 2
)
ids_conservados(proveedores, dos)
#> [1] "1-2" "3-4"
ids_conservados(invertidos, dos_invertidos)
#> [1] "1-2" "3-4"

    ⚠️ What the SQL aggregates do not translate

    sentinelas_numericos, aplicabilidad and columnas_opcionales (numeric sentinels, applicability, optional columns) change what perfil_muestra summarizes. The SQL aggregates are computed without them: AVG() knows nothing of sentinels. When any of them is declared, resumen_tabla$cobertura receives a degradado (degraded) row that says so. With 30 ages -999 declared as a sentinel, the 2 blocks publish 2 different means on the same rows:

    centinelas <- tramites
centinelas$edad[1:30] <- -999L
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "centinelas", centinelas)
declarado <- perfilar_dbi(con, "centinelas", sentinelas_numericos = -999)

media_edad <- function(cols) cols$media[cols$columna == "edad"]
c(
  resumen_sql = media_edad(columnas(declarado)),
  perfil_muestra = media_edad(columnas(declarado$perfil_muestra))
)
#>    resumen_sql perfil_muestra 
#>       34.63182       50.53385
cobertura(declarado)[, c("bloque", "elemento", "estado")]
#>          bloque             elemento    estado
#> 1 resumen_tabla sentinelas_numericos degradado

    On a perfil_dbi, columnas() returns those of the SQL summary. Those of the sample profile are requested on perfil_muestra.

    When the 2 blocks exist, perfilar_dbi() crosses them. It compares only what both measure with the same semantics. What a declaration changes on purpose stays in meta$corroboracion_bloques$no_comparadas, with its cause:

    head(declarado$resumen_tabla$meta$corroboracion_bloques$no_comparadas, 4)
#>   columna metrica                causa
#> 1    edad   media sentinelas_numericos
#> 2    edad mediana sentinelas_numericos
#> 3    edad  minimo sentinelas_numericos
#> 4    edad  maximo sentinelas_numericos

    If 2 comparable values differ beyond the tolerance, the coverage receives a divergencia (divergence) row with the 2 values. No winner is chosen. If the sample covers only part of the table, an ordinary difference is to be expected: it is declared no_corroborada (not corroborated), not divergencia.

    The tolerance is in meta$corroboracion_bloques$tolerancia:

    • for the values read, 1e-10 absolute plus 64 machine epsilons relative;
    • for the mean and the standard deviation, which each side accumulates in its own way, 1e-10 relative.

    columnas_codigo (code columns), which arrives through ..., does apply to the summary. The mean, the median and the standard deviation of a declared column stay NA, and the coverage marks them no_aplica (does not apply).

    Metrics and strategies

    metricas (metrics) chooses groups; each group publishes these fields of resumen_tabla$columnas:

    grupo campos
    "validos" n_validos, n_faltantes, prop_faltantes
    "distintos" n_distintos, tasa_distintos
    "moda" moda, frecuencia_moda
    "basicos" minimo, maximo, media, n_ceros, n_negativos
    "mediana" mediana
    "desvio" desvio

    metricas = c("validos", "basicos", "desvio") avoids the cardinality, the mode and the median, which are the queries that group or sort. metricas = "validos" leaves only completeness.

    Each row of resumen_tabla$sql carries estado, alcance, universo, tamano_muestra, fraccion, metodo and error_esperado. estado tells apart what was computed, what was estimated and what is not available, besides what was omitted for cost or for protection. In an engine sample, error_esperado (expected error) is:

    • no_estimado (not estimated) when the error could be computed under a probabilistic design, but was not computed;
    • no_estimable (not estimable) for the mode, the median and the observed cardinality;
    • no_aplica when there was no effective sampling.

    No numeric bound is published without a formula that justifies it.

    estrategia_distintos (distinct-count strategy) chooses where n_distintos comes from:

    • "exacta" (exact, the default): COUNT(DISTINCT) on the rows of the run.
    • "aproximada_motor" (engine approximation): a native function, only if the probe accepts it. Its undocumented error bounds stay as "desconocido" (unknown). If the function only knows how to build a full query, valid and distinct values are emitted separately. Each record keeps the method of the query that ran.
    • "catalogo" (catalog): pg_stats.n_distinct of PostgreSQL, published as estimado_catalogo (catalog estimate), only with universo = "tabla_completa".
    • "omitida" (omitted): it does not emit the query.

    There is no fallback between strategies: a strategy without the capability stays no_disponible and is never turned into an exact count. In SQLite, the catalog does not exist:

    por_catalogo <- perfilar_dbi(
  con, "tramites", estrategia_distintos = "catalogo",
  bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados"
)
estrategia <- por_catalogo$resumen_tabla$meta$estrategia_distintos
estrategia$estado
#> [1] "no_disponible"
writeLines(strwrap(estrategia$motivo, 88))
#> `catalogo` requiere PostgreSQL y su `pg_stats`: no hay una estadística portable de
#> cardinalidad para este motor.

    What was requested, what was resolved and the status stay in meta$estrategia_distintos and in the columns estrategia_solicitada and estrategia_resuelta of resumen_tabla$sql.

    estrategia_mediana (median strategy) enables an approximation, but does not impose it. The probe tries in this order:

    1. a consolidated exact form;
    2. an exact one per column;
    3. the approximate ones, at the end.

    resumen_tabla$sql$metodo says what ran. Only an approximation that was run stays estimado (estimated). universo = "muestra_motor" with estrategia_mediana = "aproximada_motor" is rejected on entry.

    incluir_valores = FALSE (include values) does not emit the queries of mode, extremes and median. It also clears the cell values of the summary, the sample, the blocks, the coverage and the reasons. An engine error message, which quotes the cell that caused it, is published without its literals, as with protection on. Counts and proportions are still published.

    Batched queries

    The cost of a large table is the number of passes, not the sampling. That is why the queries are grouped:

    • Flat aggregates: COUNT(col), minimum, maximum, mean, zeros, negatives and standard deviation. They travel in a single query per batch of up to tamano_lote_planos (flat batch size) columns (20 by default). In SQL Server and for float8 of PostgreSQL, the standard deviation adds a second query per batch. That way it keeps the centered computation. Each query brings COUNT(*) AS n_total_consulta: completeness uses that local denominator and not the total of another batch. The mean and the standard deviation of the decimal columns come from exact sums that the engine computes in the column’s type —the sum and the sum of the squares— and that travel in that same batch, with no extra query (with blocks, in one query of sums per batch of up to tamano_lote_planos columns). If the engine rejects a batch, it is split until the column is isolated.
    • Exact cardinalities go in their own class, in batches of tamano_lote_distintos (distinct batch size; 2 by default). Each COUNT(DISTINCT col) travels with COUNT(col) AS n_validos_guard, a control count of the same statement.
    • The mode is one query per column, because it groups. It tries to bring SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS n_validos_guard along with its frequency. The form is probed. If the engine rejects it, the query without that count is used and resumen_tabla$meta$moda_guardian declares it.
    • The median is one query per column as a fallback. If the probe accepts PERCENTILE_CONT(...) WITHIN GROUP and the percentile returns its full digits, several travel in a single SELECT per batch. The test asks for a row with a value above 1e8 and another below 1e-10, which have to come back identical. In SQL Server that requires compatibility level 110 or higher. Decimal columns do not go in that SELECT: their median is the sum of their middle values, one query per column. With bloque_filas, the mean of the decimal columns is one more query for all of them, and their median, when the two middle values fall on different doubles, one sorted query per column. MariaDB accepts the form, but returns the percentile with 10 decimals and a cap at 1e8: it uses the median per column, like MySQL. The reason for a rejection stays in meta$mediana_consolidada$motivo.
    • In the dialects with LIMIT that do not have PERCENTILE_CONT, like SQLite and PostgreSQL 9.3, the count of the median goes in a scalar subquery of the same statement. For that, the probe has to accept integer division with % and /.

    tamano_lote sets both sizes at once. The number of queries that each size produces on the table of the example, according to the plan:

    consultas_por_lote <- function(...) {
  plan <- plan_perfilado_dbi(con, "tramites", ...)
  tabla <- as.data.frame(plan)
  c(
    planos = sum(tabla$n_consultas[grepl("planos", tabla$clase_consulta)]),
    distintos = sum(tabla$n_consultas[grepl("distintos", tabla$clase_consulta)]),
    total = attr(plan, "total")
  )
}
rbind(
  planos_1 = consultas_por_lote(tamano_lote_planos = 1),
  por_omision = consultas_por_lote(),
  distintos_1 = consultas_por_lote(tamano_lote_distintos = 1),
  distintos_4 = consultas_por_lote(tamano_lote_distintos = 4)
)
#>             planos distintos total
#> planos_1         6         2    24
#> por_omision      3         2    21
#> distintos_1      3         4    23
#> distintos_4      3         1    20

    The value of tamano_lote_distintos is an assumption of the code, noted next to the constant (R/perfilar-dbi.R). In PostgreSQL, the read of the table is the same with any batch. The engine amortizes a pass among the aggregates of the same SELECT. What grows with the batch is the spill to disk of PostgreSQL. The optimum depends on work_mem, which changes by server. To choose another value, instrumentar = TRUE publishes the duration of each query.

    If a batch fails, the batch is not lost. Its halves are probed by bisection:

    • the accepted groups are reused as measurements;
    • the culprit columns are retried by metric, with their local denominator;
    • what still fails stays no_disponible with its reason.

    If the budget runs out before isolating everything, the pending columns stay unmeasured. They are not assumed to be culprits or readable. meta$tamano_lote_funciono keeps the largest batch accepted in that run. No state tied to the connection is kept.

    resumen_tabla$sql adds lote and columnas_compartidas to see which query was shared. The order of degradation is:

    1. flat aggregates;
    2. total of the universe, when needed;
    3. distinct values;
    4. mode;
    5. median.

    Cost policy

    The mode and the median are the expensive metrics. politica_costo (cost policy) accepts 2 values, and no other:

    tryCatch(
  perfilar_dbi(con, "tramites", politica_costo = "ninguna"),
  error = function(e) writeLines(strwrap(conditionMessage(e), 88))
)
#> `politica_costo` debe ser un único valor: `todas` o `por_cardinalidad`.
    • "todas" (all, the default) keeps mode and median in all the requested columns. The package does not choose for the user.
    • "por_cardinalidad" (by cardinality) first resolves the structural sources: a guaranteed primary key says how many distinct values there are without counting them. It measures validos and distintos only if needed and if the strategy allows it. Then it omits, per column, only the mode, when n_distintos / n_validos >= umbral_cardinalidad. The threshold is 0.5 by default and can be moved in each call. The median is not omitted by cardinality: its cost is governed by the rows.
    barato <- perfilar_dbi(con, "tramites", politica_costo = "por_cardinalidad")
s <- sql_perfil(barato)
s[s$estado == "omitido_por_costo", c("columna", "metrica", "estado")]
#>       columna         metrica            estado
#> 10 id_tramite            moda omitido_por_costo
#> 11 id_tramite frecuencia_moda omitido_por_costo
#> 38      monto            moda omitido_por_costo
#> 39      monto frecuencia_moda omitido_por_costo
writeLines(strwrap(barato$resumen_tabla$meta$decisiones_costo$monto$detalle$motivo, 88))
#> Se omitió la moda de la columna `monto`: tiene 2000 valores distintos de 2000 válidos
#> (1.000) sobre la tabla completa; la política optativa considera que agrupar u ordenar
#> toda la columna no justifica el costo. Para pedirla igual, usar `politica_costo =
#> "todas"`; para mover el criterio, cambiar `umbral_cardinalidad`.

    On a wider table, the difference shows in the number of queries. The table that follows has 200 rows and 158 columns:

    • numeric: 60;
    • text: 60;
    • integer: 20;
    • dates stored as text: 18.

    It is the same one that benchmark/medir_plan_ancho.R and benchmark/medir_politica_costo.R use:

    set.seed(1)
filas <- 200
generar <- function(prefijo, k, valores) {
  stats::setNames(lapply(seq_len(k), function(i) valores()), paste0(prefijo, seq_len(k)))
}
ancha <- as.data.frame(c(
  generar("num", 60, function() round(stats::rnorm(filas) * 100, 2)),
  generar("txt", 60, function() sample(letters, filas, replace = TRUE)),
  generar("ent", 20, function() sample(seq_len(50L), filas, replace = TRUE)),
  generar("fec", 18, function() {
    as.character(as.Date("2026-01-01") - sample(seq_len(900L), filas, replace = TRUE))
  })
))
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "ancha", ancha)

corrida <- function(politica) {
  perfilar_dbi(
    con, "ancha", bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados", instrumentar = FALSE,
    politica_costo = politica, proteger_datos_personales = FALSE
  )
}
emitidas_ancha <- function(x) x$resumen_tabla$meta$consultas$emitidas
todas <- corrida("todas")
por_cardinalidad <- corrida("por_cardinalidad")
por_politica <- c(
  todas = emitidas_ancha(todas),
  por_cardinalidad = emitidas_ancha(por_cardinalidad)
)
por_politica
#>            todas por_cardinalidad 
#>              334              256

    With "por_cardinalidad", the run saved 78 of 334 queries, all of them of mode.

    The structural sources are resolved whenever the policy needs the cardinality, even if estrategia_distintos is omitted or not available. The strategy decides whether it can be measured, but does not hide a guaranteed primary key. If there is no structural source and the strategy does not allow measuring, the cardinality stays unknown. Then the policy follows its rule for that case.

    Each omission stays in resumen_tabla$sql as omitido_por_costo (omitted for cost). It says what was omitted, why and how to request it again (politica_costo = "todas" or another threshold). meta$decisiones_costo explains separately the decision on each metric of each column.

    fuente_cardinalidad_costo says where the proportion came from, and is independent of estrategia_distintos. The policy never turns a request "aproximada_motor" or "catalogo" into an exact COUNT(DISTINCT).

    ⏱ The plan before running

    plan_perfilado_dbi() emits only preparation queries:

    • the schema;
    • the capability probes;
    • the catalog of the primary key;
    • in PostgreSQL, its statistics.

    It says how many queries the profiling would emit, of which class and with which scope. It does not scan data to decide the cost.

    plan <- plan_perfilado_dbi(con, "tramites")
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(plan))
    clase_consulta n_consultas alcance n_consultas_max
    portones (esquema y sondas) 7 una vez 7
    agregados planos por lotes (COUNT + MIN/MAX/AVG/SUM CASE + desvio) 3 escanea la tabla completa 3
    distintos por lotes (clase separada) 2 escanea la tabla completa 2
    moda (GROUP BY + orden + limite) 4 ordena o agrupa la tabla completa 4
    mediana (orden total + limite/salto) 3 ordena la tabla completa 3
    muestra 2 lee las filas pedidas 2

    The cost is a range:

    • attr(plan, "total") (21 here) counts the queries if no batch is rejected. With politica_costo = "por_cardinalidad", it assumes that the mode whose cardinality is not known is omitted.
    • attr(plan, "total_maximo") (34) adds the path that runs that mode and the bisection probes, if the engine rejected every batch. They are up to 2n − 1 per batch of n columns. total_lotes_rechazados publishes the same number.

    The default run of the example emitted 21.

    The range holds when the sampling can be built. If universo = "muestra_motor" and the form cannot be built, attr(plan, "muestreo") declares it and the plan excludes those metrics. In status "no_sondeado" (not probed), the form was only built locally. The range stays conditional on the probe of the run accepting it.

    The plan counts what max_consultas and meta$consultas$emitidas count: every statement the profile sends to the engine, except the transaction guard and the pg_stat_statements reads of instrumentar. With bloque_filas it counts the preparation, the scan and the queries that follow; those the data ask for —the median of a decimal whose central values are distinct doubles, its centred standard deviation, the retry of a short TABLESAMPLE— go to total_maximo. With max_consultas = attr(plan, "total_maximo") no metric is left out by the budget.

    The count follows the composition of the table, not the number of columns. With the wide table of the previous section and one of 158 columns, all of them text:

    plan_ancho <- plan_perfilado_dbi(con, "ancha")
recorre <- !as.character(plan_ancho$alcance) %in% c("una vez", "lee las filas pedidas")
texto <- as.data.frame(generar("txt", 158, function() sample(letters, filas, replace = TRUE)))
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "ancha_texto", texto)
c(
  ancha = attr(plan_ancho, "total"),
  ancha_recorren_la_tabla = sum(plan_ancho$n_consultas[recorre]),
  solo_texto = attr(plan_perfilado_dbi(con, "ancha_texto"), "total")
)
#>                   ancha ancha_recorren_la_tabla              solo_texto 
#>                     336                     327                     255

    Of the 336 queries of the wide table, 327 scan, sort or group the whole table. Text columns cost less, above all because the median —which sorts the table— is requested only on numeric columns. muestra bounds none of that: it bounds what is brought into R, not the work of the engine. benchmark/medir_plan_ancho.R redoes these figures and leaves a dated output with the environment.

    Each capability probe spends a fixed number of queries even if it succeeds with the first form. It is a design decision. If the cost varied by engine, the plan could not say exactly how many queries it is going to emit.

    Counting queries does not say how much they cost: 14 queries on 2 million rows are more work than 200 on 1,000. The plan also estimates the magnitude, in 2 halves:

    • the one of the engine: filas_leidas and ordenaciones_completas, summarized in magnitud_motor;
    • the one of the client: columnas_texto and pares_texto, summarized in magnitud_texto. pares_texto are the pairs of forms that the vocabulary detector could compare in R on the sample.

    magnitud (magnitude) is the larger of the 2: "baja", "media", "alta" (low, medium, high), or "desconocida" (unknown) if the number of rows is not known. The plan does not count rows. Only in PostgreSQL, a positive pg_class.reltuples provides a catalog estimate, labeled as such. In SQLite it stays unknown:

    attr(plan, "magnitud")
#> [1] "desconocida"
num(attr(plan, "pares_texto"))
#> [1] "2.000.000"

    The magnitude is an estimate:

    • the one of the engine counts the rows that would have to be read if no index helped;
    • the one of the client counts pairs. Its cost depends on the length of the values, which the plan does not know without reading them.

    Printing the plan shows the 2 halves, the high-work warning and the levers to bound it. That text cites reference speeds of other runs to turn counts into seconds. They are assumptions of the code, not measurements of the table.

    The plan does not project seconds for COUNT(DISTINCT): without reading data it has no measured reference. With universo = "muestra_motor", the plan also declares the local copy:

    • attr(plan, "materializacion"): the single selection that will be paid, with pagado = FALSE;
    • attr(plan, "pasadas"): the passes that will read that copy.

    ⚠️ Cost and spill warnings

    The warnings of perfilar_dbi() also arrive in non-interactive scripts, because the cost is paid on the server. Each one has its switch and its threshold. Turning it off does not turn off the measurement or its metadata.

    warning how it projects when it warns where it stays
    COUNT(DISTINCT) median of the durations of the first batch of distinct values of this run, times the number of batches after the first batch and before the second, if there is more than one and the projection reaches umbral_segundos_aviso_distintos meta$costo_distintos
    mode ms per distinct value of the first mode measured, times the cardinality of the others before the next mode meta$costo_moda
    median ms per row of the first median measured before the pending medians meta$costo_mediana
    estimated spill (PostgreSQL) size of the hash with pg_stats and pg_class.reltuples against work_mem before the first COUNT(DISTINCT) meta$estimacion_derrame

    The 3 time thresholds are 30 seconds by default, and Inf turns off each warning explicitly. With a single batch of distinct values there is nothing to project. The projection of distinct values does not use reltuples. If the mode has no cardinality, the projection declares it instead of assuming it.

    costo <- por_omision$resumen_tabla$meta$costo_distintos
str(costo[c("disponible", "n_lotes")])
#> List of 2
#>  $ disponible: logi TRUE
#>  $ n_lotes   : int 2
writeLines(strwrap(costo$fuente, 88))
#> mediana de 1 consulta del primer lote de distintos medido en esta corrida

    When a total median does not leave a local measurement, the projection uses a reference of 68 ms per million rows. It is a constant of the code taken from another run, with no script that redoes it. It is not presented as a measurement of the current run. If the query that counted the rows was measured and gives a larger bound, that bound is published separately, as an observed reading.

    In PostgreSQL, the preparation also reads:

    • pg_stats.n_distinct and pg_stats.avg_width;
    • pg_class.reltuples;
    • work_mem and, since PostgreSQL 13, hash_mem_multiplier.

    If the estimated hash exceeds the effective limit, it warns that raising work_mem in the session can avoid the spill. The package does not change the configuration or wait for confirmation.

    The estimate of the mode uses EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON, COSTS OFF) without ANALYZE. The one of the median models a sort with minimums of 32 bytes per value for fixed types and 42 for numeric.

    With instrumentar = TRUE and pg_stat_statements available, the measured spill —temporary blocks written and read— prevails over the estimate. If the call cannot be attributed, the status stays not available: the elapsed time is not presented as evidence of spill.

    The block perfil_muestra goes through perfilar(), and in an interactive session it also receives its wide-table warning.

    Wide tables

    Before starting the expensive stages, perfilar() projects how long a table can take from its number of cells. From 100,000 cells it warns of the estimated duration, only in an interactive session. The projection is always kept:

    str(ajustado$meta$costo_tabla_ancha[c(
  "celdas", "duracion_estimada_segundos", "umbral_celdas"
)])
#> List of 3
#>  $ celdas                    : num 32
#>  $ duracion_estimada_segundos: num 0.0064
#>  $ umbral_celdas             : int 100000

    The duration comes from dividing the cells by a reference speed of 5,000 cells per second. It stays below the slowest measurement of benchmark/medir_referencias.R: 8,044 cells per second, with 500 rows and numeric and categorical columns.

    It is a reference for the common case, not a bound. benchmark/medir_topes_valores_ancho.R measures equal columns of text codes ("valor_1", "valor_2"…), with the near-duplicate search of the vocabulary turned off. As all the columns are equal, the profile publishes a single columnas_duplicadas finding that names them all. Its slowest case is 9,754 cells per second, also above the reference.

    The 2 CSV files, in benchmark/datos/, keep the date, the environment and the fingerprint of the code. The warning is turned off with avisar_costo_tabla_ancha = FALSE, and umbral_celdas_aviso_tabla_ancha = Inf is the same decision, explicit.

    The dated measurements of wide tables are in Evidencia y rendimiento (Evidence and performance, in Spanish). They are the query plan of an administrative table of 158 columns and the 2 tables of speed.

    Instrumentation and durations

    With instrumentar = TRUE (the default in the run), each row of resumen_tabla$sql adds these fields:

    • duracion_ms, which uses Sys.time();
    • cpu_ms, which adds proc.time()[c("user.self", "sys.self")] and measures the CPU work of the client, including the conversion of the result that the driver does;
    • n_filas_resultado and bytes_resultado_r;
    • consulta_id, etapa and nivel.

    A 0 is measured; an NA, not measured. With instrumentar = FALSE the same queries are emitted in the same order, and those fields stay NA.

    duracion_ms is the duration of the query, repeated in each row that query produced. To add up, only the rows of nivel = 1 (level) count, the first of each consulta_id:

    s <- sql_perfil(por_omision)
table(s$nivel, useNA = "ifany")
#> 
#>  1  2 
#> 17 43
length(unique(stats::na.omit(s$consulta_id)))
#> [1] 10
    sum(s$duracion_ms[s$nivel == 1], na.rm = TRUE)

    There are 2 identifiers that answer different questions:

    • consulta_id identifies the statement that produced each measurement within the run, and defines the consistency group.
    • id_consulta identifies the data query: 2 metrics with the same value saw exactly the same rows. It does not depend on instrumentar, and it is NA in the mode and the median, which do not share rows with other metrics.

    memoria_trabajo (working memory) classifies the working state of the engine as creciente (growing), acotado (bounded) or NA.

    resumen_tabla$tiempos gathers the large stages of the client in the same unit. Those of nivel = 1 are disjoint; those of a higher level are contained in one of them:

    por_omision$resumen_tabla$tiempos[, c("etapa", "nivel", "estado")]
#>                            etapa nivel        estado
#> 1           ausencia_estructural     2        medido
#> 2    casi_duplicados_vocabulario     2        medido
#> 3 clasificacion_datos_personales     2        medido
#> 4                   dependencias     2        medido
#> 5         duplicados_aproximados     2 no_solicitado
#> 6                lectura_muestra     1        medido
#> 7             perfilado_columnas     2        medido
#> 8              perfilado_muestra     1        medido
#> 9    proteccion_datos_personales     2 no_solicitado

    In an interactive session, a bar advances against the queries that the plan expects to emit. options(lupa.progreso = FALSE) turns it off and TRUE forces it. It does not change any measured value.

    Processing memory

    plan_perfilado_dbi() does not estimate the processing memory in R, and declares it:

    memoria <- attr(plan, "memoria_procesamiento")
memoria$estado
#> [1] "no_estimada"
writeLines(strwrap(memoria$motivo, 88))
#> no escala de forma predecible con las filas ni con las celdas; se midió.

    The attribute keeps 2 things:

    • the known magnitude of the work (rows, cells and text pairs), labeled as magnitude and not as consumption;
    • references of other runs, which are fixed texts of the code.
    names(memoria)
#> [1] "estado"            "estimada"          "motivo"            "magnitud"         
#> [5] "referencias"       "distincion"        "reparto_observado"
names(memoria$referencias)
#> [1] "traer"     "procesar"  "variacion"

    Those references say how much it cost to bring the rows, how much to process them in R and how much that varied between tables. They come from a single run, dated 2026-08-28, against a remote production engine, and this repository cannot redo it.

    They are not a prediction for the table of the plan. They are not used to estimate because they vary between tables of the same magnitude. print(plan) shows them, and the figures with their source are in Evidencia y rendimiento (Evidence and performance, in Spanish).

    Seeing every row and holding them all in memory is not the same. There are 3 recipes, depending on what is needed:

    need configuration
    bounded aggregates, without rows in R universo = "muestra_motor", muestra_motor = n, bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados"
    row-level findings muestra = n, with orden_muestra if the read has to be reproducible, and the caps on cells and bytes
    summary of the whole table without retaining it bloque_filas = n

    A run on production databases

    Between 26 and 30 October 2026, an external team ran perfilar_dbi() on 8 production databases:

    • PostgreSQL: 5 databases, from 9.3 to 13;
    • SQL Server: 3 databases, 2008 R2 and 2016.

    The machine had 121 GB of memory and R 4.5.2. They are figures of a single run, with the version of those dates and on data that the repository does not have. They are not redone from here and are not extrapolated to another machine.

    Small tables, single path Aggregates (tabla_completa) Engine sample
    Median 0.6 s 12 s 26 s
    99th percentile 47 s 1,822 s 323 s

    There were 3,709 calls on 3,316 tables, and 3,693 finished fine. Another 3 finished with a warning. Of the remaining 13, 11 were cut by the maximum time that the team set and 2, by an error of the process. The median memory of a call was between 230 and 530 MB depending on the path. On those profiles, reportar() took a median of 0.06 s and planificar_limpieza(), 0.008 s.

    The protection of personal data was measured on 3 tables of up to 100,000 rows, with the same call with and without proteger_datos_personales = TRUE. It cost between 11% and 18% more time, with a memory between 5% lower and 11% higher. Each of those calls drew its own engine sample, so the rows were not exactly the same. The engine and the driver also take their share. The protection is a cost in the low double digits, not a null cost.

    The slowest parts of that run were fixed afterwards. Each fix was measured on a local reproduction, not on those databases, and the run on them is still to be repeated:

    • the standard deviation in SQL Server, which went in one query per column, each one on the whole table, goes in batches (Batched queries): on a million rows and 27 numeric columns it went from 27 queries to 2, and from 1.42 million logical reads to 105 thousand, with the same figures;
    • the date columns in R before 4.6: 100,000 dates went from 171 s to 1.3 s in R 4.5.2;
    • the very long texts: 700 rows of four 14 KB columns went from 23 s to 5 s;
    • the engine sample, which could bring into R more than its budget: 200 rows of 1.25 MB of text and binary reach the spool in 27 KB (Caps on the read into R).

    The first three figures are in the NEWS.md entry of each fix.

    The agreement of the figures with an SQL count written separately is in Evidencia y rendimiento (Evidence and performance, in Spanish).

    Consistency across queries

    The aggregates are separate statements, and the table can change between them. The summary publishes it:

    por_omision$resumen_tabla$meta$snapshot
#> [1] FALSE
writeLines(strwrap(por_omision$resumen_tabla$meta$nota_snapshot, 88))
#> No hubo lectura instantánea: cada agregado se midió en su propio momento y la tabla
#> pudo cambiar entre consultas. La cobertura declara las comparaciones incoherentes entre
#> grupos de consistencia distintos.

    The hard bounds are checked only within one statement:

    • the frequency of the mode, against its control count;
    • the distinct values, against the n_validos_guard of their own query.

    If exact n_validos and n_distintos are inconsistent and come from different statements, the coverage adds an alcance_distinto (different scope) row. Its reason names the 2 statements. It is evidence that the table changed during the run, not an accusation against the engine or the package. If an approximation cannot bring the control count, the check is declared as not available.

    With universo = "muestra_motor" and bloque_muestra = "con_muestra", the selection of the engine runs only once. It is kept in a local copy: a temporary file of the R session (the spool). The whole profile reads that copy and never samples the engine again.

    On each reread, a closing record checks muestra_id, snapshot_id, orden_id, n_filas, bytes and the checksum. A missing record publishes spool_incompleto:trailer_ausente, and a checksum that does not match, spool_checksum_invalido. The copy does not write to the connection or create temporary objects in the engine:

    copia <- del_motor$resumen_tabla$meta$materializacion
str(copia[c("backend", "estado", "externo", "objetos_temporales_motor",
            "validado_relectura")])
#> List of 5
#>  $ backend                 : chr "spool_sesion_cliente"
#>  $ estado                  : chr "cerrada_verificada"
#>  $ externo                 : logi TRUE
#>  $ objetos_temporales_motor: logi FALSE
#>  $ validado_relectura      : logi TRUE

    Rereading the copy can cost more than asking the engine for the selection again on each pass. It is chosen because it guarantees that every metric describes the same rows. snapshot_id identifies the copy of the client, not a transactional snapshot of the engine.

    For a consistent read, the path can run inside a transaction opened by the user. That user sets the isolation level the engine needs. The package never sends BEGIN, COMMIT or ROLLBACK. Outside a transaction, it does not add statements of that kind. The same holds for plan_perfilado_dbi(), perfilar_coleccion() (profile a collection) and relaciones_coleccion() (collection relationships).

    engine inside a transaction
    PostgreSQL an error aborts the transaction, so each statement goes between its own SAVEPOINT and its RELEASE, with ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT if it fails
    SQL Server it can roll back the transaction on an error; the path measures @@TRANCOUNT and XACT_STATE() before and after each send and read, and if they change it raises lupa_error_transaccion_dbi
    MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite the error of a query does not abort the transaction
    DuckDB an error while preparing aborts it and there is no SAVEPOINT: a view that fails leaves the transaction aborted, and it has to be closed with ROLLBACK

    Dialects and probes

    Bounding rows is not standard SQL. Before emitting the aggregates, perfilar_dbi() probes the engine with a query that returns no rows. It chooses the first capability that the engine accepts:

    dialecto forma motores
    "limit" LIMIT n [OFFSET k] PostgreSQL, SQLite, MySQL/MariaDB, DuckDB y compatibles
    "top" TOP (n), y OFFSET k ROWS FETCH NEXT n ROWS ONLY con orden SQL Server 2012 o posterior, Sybase
    "fetch_first" OFFSET k ROWS FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY Oracle 12c o posterior, DB2, Derby, H2
    "rownum" ROWNUM <= n; no expresa salto Oracle anterior a 12c
    "portable" sin cláusula de límite: se acota con dbSendQuery() y dbFetch(n) cualquier motor con DBI 
    dialecto <- por_omision$resumen_tabla$meta$dialecto
str(dialecto[c("nombre", "declarado")])
#> List of 2
#>  $ nombre   : chr "limit"
#>  $ declarado: logi FALSE
writeLines(strwrap(dialecto$sondas, 88))
#> SELECT `id_tramite`, `categoria`, `monto`, `edad` FROM `tramites` WHERE 1 = 0 LIMIT 1

    If no capability works, the portable path remains, which bounds in the client with dbSendQuery() and dbFetch(n). There the exact median is declared not available, instead of bringing half a table into memory. If the probe gets it wrong, dialecto = (dialect) declares the capability without probing:

    portable <- perfilar_dbi(con, "tramites", dialecto = "portable",
                         bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados")
s <- sql_perfil(portable)
writeLines(strwrap(s$motivo[s$columna == "monto" & s$metrica == "mediana"], 88))
#> NA

    Each probe tries the same form that is emitted afterwards. A cheaper form is not enough: an engine can accept a clause with a trivially false filter and reject it without it. DuckDB does it with block sampling:

    probar <- function(sql) {
  tryCatch({ DBI::dbGetQuery(duck, sql); "aceptada" },
           error = function(e) "rechazada")
}
c(
  con_filtro_falso = probar("SELECT 1 FROM t TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM (10) WHERE 1 = 0"),
  sin_filtro = probar("SELECT 1 FROM t TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM (10)")
)
#> con_filtro_falso       sin_filtro 
#>       "aceptada"       "aceptada"

    Other rules of the dialect:

    • The subquery alias is written with AS or without it, depending on the engine. The column aliases go between quotes and are compared without case sensitivity, because there are engines that fold them.
    • The median under muestra_motor uses a single CTE with COUNT(*) OVER () and ROW_NUMBER() OVER in 2 cases: in the dialects without a consolidated or scalar form (MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server with compatibility below 110) and in each column that cannot use the consolidated one (a float8 of PostgreSQL, a column with extremes). It chooses the 2 central positions without dividing and, with extremes, averages them without overflowing within the same statement. Its probe repeats that construction on SELECT 1.0 UNION ALL ... SELECT 4.0, and requires 2.5 and a negative control that fails. The production table is not probed. With dialecto = "portable", which has no row skipping, the median of the whole table also comes from that CTE.
    • With the driver recognized, the syntax probes of other engines are not run. In SQL Server with XACT_ABORT ON, a statement that does not belong would abort the transaction.

    What the engine stores differently from R

    The SQL summary describes what the engine has in front of it, and sometimes it is not the same as the table in R. The full detail is in the section «Lo que el motor guarda distinto que R» of ?perfilar_dbi. The known cases, with what the package publishes:

    engine what happens what lupa publishes
    SQLite it has no date type: a Date is stored as days since 1970 without more information it describes it as a number; with extended_types = TRUE when connecting, the column is temporal and receives no quantitative aggregates
    SQLite a column of numeric affinity admits text, and RSQLite reads it as 0 it counts with typeof() the values stored as text or blob and declares the divergence with that cause
    DuckDB NaN is a value: it counts as present and distinct, and MAX or AVG answer NaN a metric answered with NaN stays no_disponible with its reason
    SQLite, PostgreSQL, DuckDB Inf and -Inf enter MIN, MAX, AVG and the median the magnitude statistics are requested again on the finite values, as in perfilar()
    PostgreSQL RPostgres reads 0 in every money cell, and a real through its text both are read converted in the engine; the conversion stays in meta$lectura_convertida
    PostgreSQL 9.3 to 11, or extra_float_digits <= 0 the text of a double precision has fewer digits the read decodes the 8 bytes of the value with float8send()
    SQL Server datetimeoffset can arrive converted to UTC by FreeTDS the lost offset is not rebuilt; the corroboration leaves it as a divergence
    SQL Server STDEV accumulates in one pass and loses digits with large means the standard deviation is requested on the values centered on the mean
    SQL Server it does not admit COUNT(DISTINCT), GROUP BY, ORDER BY or MIN/MAX on text, ntext, image, xml and geography those metrics stay no_disponible without sending the statement
    any the collation of the column groups values that R tells apart (COLLATE NOCASE, non-deterministic ICU, trailing spaces in SQL Server) meta$criterio_comparacion and meta$criterio_moda declare it; the corroboration leaves it no_corroborada, not divergencia
    any 64-bit integers (or HUGEINT and UHUGEINT in DuckDB) or decimals that arrive as double from 2^53 the magnitude metrics that depend on a value a double cannot represent stay no_disponible (minimo, maximo, media, desvio, n_ceros and n_negativos). The median is published when its value is exact: with an odd count, if the middle value is below 2^53; with an even count, if both middle values lie between -2^52 and 2^52, which costs one more query on the full table. perfil_muestra, the sample read into R and perfilar() decide it from its middle values, which they see: it is published when they fit in a double. The mode is requested from the engine as exact text; the sample reads those columns as text and, with bit64, as integer64
    any a decimal with more digits than a double holds arrives as a double on the full table and with blocks, the mean and the standard deviation come from the sum of the column and the sum of the squares of its differences from the mean, which the engine computes in the column’s type and returns as text; with the sample read into R, the mean, the median and the standard deviation come from each value’s text, and the block median from the middle values the engine returns as text; on the engine sample with solo_agregados, from the same sums, requested in the statement of the aggregates. The perfil_muestra standard deviation follows the rule of the doubles on every path: it is not published, it is listed in perfil_muestra$meta$desvio_decimal_doble, and the cross-check does not compare it (cause decimal_doble)
    MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, DuckDB AVG(x * 1.0) of a decimal is cut at the engine’s maximum scale (30, 38), PERCENTILE_CONT interpolates in double, and averaging in R the doubles of two middle values is not exact a decimal’s median sums its middle values in the engine and R divides by how many there are: one query per decimal column
    SQL Server CAST(x AS VARCHAR) is VARCHAR(30), and writes money with two decimals the sample reads a decimal’s text as VARCHAR(48) and money with CONVERT(..., 2)
    DuckDB AVG(x * 1.0) overflows with a HUGEINT from 10^37 or a UHUGEINT from 10^38 the basics are requested again without the average; the mean stays no_disponible and the rest is judged as in any column
    DuckDB PERCENTILE_CONT interpolates a DECIMAL in its own scale and truncates, and the driver converts a decimal of more than 18 digits to a double that is not the nearest the median of a DECIMAL goes by the sum of its middle values, read through its text
    PostgreSQL PERCENTILE_CONT interpolates low + (high - low) * 0.5 in double with an even count and middle values more than 2^53 apart, the median stays no_disponible (that of a numeric goes by the sum of its middle values and is published)
    SQL Server decimal - literal beyond 38 digits is rounded, and from compatibility level 110 a tie rounds away from zero the center of a decimal’s standard deviation never ends in 5
    SQLite RSQLite returns integer or integer64 depending on the values of each block with bloque_filas, blocks are joined as integer64 before counting distinct values, mode and median
    SQLite the window mean of the sample is a rounded double the sum of squares subtracts n * (mean - center)^2
    any each engine adds up in its own way, and with values that cancel out the means differ between engines and from the one of R the mean is requested as double where decimal arithmetic would cut it; the corroboration declares the difference

    The mean of {1e16, 1, -1e16} is 1/3. Each path computes it in its own way, and none is taken as true:

    cancelan <- data.frame(x = c(1e16, 1, -1e16))
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "cancelan", cancelan)
DBI::dbWriteTable(duck, "cancelan", cancelan)
c(
  sqlite = DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT AVG(x) FROM cancelan")[[1]],
  duckdb = DBI::dbGetQuery(duck, "SELECT AVG(x) FROM cancelan")[[1]],
  r = mean(cancelan$x)
)
#>    sqlite    duckdb         r 
#> 0.3333333 0.0000000 0.3336589

    When the 2 blocks exist and differ beyond the tolerance, the corroboration leaves the divergencia row with the 2 values.

    In SQLite, the difference of the dates shows like this:

    fechas <- data.frame(f = as.Date("2019-03-01") + 0:9)
perfilar_fechas <- function(...) {
  base <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:", ...)
  on.exit(DBI::dbDisconnect(base))
  DBI::dbWriteTable(base, "fechas", fechas)
  x <- perfilar_dbi(base, "fechas", bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados",
                    proteger_datos_personales = FALSE)
  columnas(x)[, c("columna", "minimo", "maximo", "media")]
}
perfilar_fechas()
#>   columna minimo maximo   media
#> 1       f  17956  17965 17960.5
perfilar_fechas(extended_types = TRUE)
#>   columna minimo maximo media
#> 1       f     NA     NA    NA

    The primary key by engine

    The primary key is not guessed: it is read from the catalog of the engine. That metadata query does not go through the table, and it is done in every run, with any cost policy. The answer stays in resumen_tabla$meta$clave, with columnas, fuente, motivo, garantia and estado. garantia (guarantee) is garantizada (guaranteed), declarada_no_garantizada (declared, not guaranteed), desconocida (unknown) or no_declarada (not declared). A failed query keeps its reason and is not confused with a table without a key.

    With an unqualified name, the key published is the one of the relation that the engine resolves, with its same schema rules. A key whose columns are not among the ones just measured is discarded whole, in any engine, and the reason is given.

    What each catalog can state:

    engine catalog path garantizada when
    PostgreSQL pg_catalog the constraint is enforced and validated, without child tables by inheritance (partitions do not count), it is not DEFERRABLE and its index is unique; otherwise, declarada_no_garantizada
    MySQL information_schema ENFORCED is YES
    Oracle all_constraints STATUS is ENABLED, it is VALIDATED and it is not DEFERRABLE (tested with a simulated engine)
    SQLite pragma all the columns of the key are NOT NULL; otherwise, uniqueness among non-null values is guaranteed but the guarantee stays desconocida
    MariaDB show_index never: the catalog does not expose a comparable status and the guarantee stays desconocida
    SQL Server information_schema never: it stays desconocida
    DuckDB duckdb_constraints never: it stays desconocida 
    crear <- function(conexion, sql) invisible(DBI::dbExecute(conexion, sql))
crear(con, "CREATE TABLE con_nulos (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, x TEXT)")
crear(con, "CREATE TABLE sin_nulos (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, x TEXT)")
crear(con, "CREATE TABLE sin_clave (id INTEGER, x TEXT)")
crear(duck, "CREATE TABLE padron (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, x VARCHAR)")
leer_clave <- function(conexion, tabla) {
  x <- perfilar_dbi(conexion, tabla, bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados")
  k <- x$resumen_tabla$meta$clave
  data.frame(tabla = tabla, columnas = paste(k$columnas, collapse = ", "),
             fuente = k$fuente, garantia = k$garantia)
}
rbind(
  leer_clave(con, "con_nulos"),
  leer_clave(con, "sin_nulos"),
  leer_clave(con, "sin_clave"),
  leer_clave(duck, "padron")
)
#>       tabla columnas             fuente     garantia
#> 1 con_nulos       id             pragma  desconocida
#> 2 sin_nulos       id             pragma  garantizada
#> 3 sin_clave                      pragma no_declarada
#> 4    padron       id duckdb_constraints  desconocida

    With politica_costo = "por_cardinalidad", a guaranteed key says how many distinct values its column has without counting them. The check of a key that the user declares on data in memory (perfilar(clave = ...)) is in Leer un perfil (Reading a profile, in Spanish). The key suggestions are there too.

    🗄️ Tested engines

    The matrix is assembled when the page is built, with the output of benchmark/verificar_motor.R: the file benchmark/datos/verificar-motor.csv. Each row is an engine of the same run, with:

    • the engine and the version that the server reports;
    • the R driver and its version;
    • the result of each check: ok, or fallo (failure) with the message.

    Below go the date of the run, the revision of the package measured and the fixture. An engine that did not respond stays no_medido (not measured), with its reason.

    motor servidor controlador estado cinco columnas dialecto media clave primaria cobertura
    PostgreSQL 16 16.15 RPostgres 1.4.10 medido ok ok ok ok ok
    PostgreSQL 9.3 9.3.25 RPostgres 1.4.10 medido ok ok ok ok ok
    MySQL 8.4 8.4.11 RMySQL 0.11.3 medido ok ok ok ok ok
    MariaDB 11.8 11.8.8 RMariaDB 1.3.5 medido ok ok ok ok ok
    SQL Server 2022 16.0.4265.3 odbc/FreeTDS 1.7.0 medido ok ok ok ok ok
    SQLite 3.53.3 RSQLite 3.53.3 medido ok ok ok ok ok
    DuckDB 1.5.5 duckdb 1.5.5 medido ok ok ok ok ok

    Corrida del 2026-10-24T13:12:59Z (UTC), sobre la revisión 0.1.0; R/ md5 08c0a1af7ccb del paquete. Fixture declarado por el guion: «tramites: cinco columnas; padron: clave primaria id_persona».

    What benchmark/verificar_motor.R does:

    • It is run from the root of the source code: Rscript benchmark/verificar_motor.R [motores]. Without arguments it goes through the 7 engines of the matrix (postgres16, postgres93, mysql84, mariadb118, sqlserver2022, sqlite and duckdb). With arguments, only the named ones.
    • It loads the package from the source with pkgload, if available: it measures the code of the tree and not the installed package.
    • It does not take an arbitrary connection: each engine has its connection written in the script. SQLite and DuckDB go in memory; the others, in local containers with their own ports. The passwords of MySQL, MariaDB and SQL Server are read from LUPA_MYSQL_PWD, LUPA_MARIADB_PWD and LUPA_MSSQL_PWD. For another server or another engine, its connection has to be added to the script or the checks repeated by hand.
    • It writes the fixture in each engine, and profiles tramites with the call that follows this list. The fixture has 2 tables:
      • tramites, of 500 rows and 5 columns: identifier, document, category, amount and age with 20 missing values;
      • padron, with primary key id_persona declared NOT NULL.
    • It makes 5 checks:
      • that the summary has 5 columns;
      • that the dialect was resolved;
      • that the mean of monto of the engine matches the one of R on the same column, with relative tolerance of 1e-8;
      • that the primary key of padron is read from the catalog as id_persona;
      • that resumen_tabla$cobertura is a table.
    • It ends with a non-zero code if any check fails.
    perfilar_dbi(
  con, "tramites", muestra = 500L, analizar_dependencias = FALSE,
  duplicados_aproximados = FALSE, proteger_datos_personales = FALSE
)

    It does not check how many metrics are computed or how many stay no_aplica, nor does it time anything. The check of the mean holds for finite values of ordinary scale, like those of the fixture. With NaN, infinities or sums that lose precision, the engine and R do not match. That is declared by the corroboration between blocks (above).

    What is not in the run:

    case status source
    engine that rejects LIMIT (the case of SQL Server, whose real matrix does not exercise that rejection) tested with a simulated engine tests/testthat/test-arreglos-dbi.R
    engine that folds the aliases to upper case, like Oracle, DB2, Firebird or Snowflake tested with a simulated engine tests/testthat/test-arreglos-dbi.R
    engine that rejects a column (a LOB that the driver does not materialize, a per-column permission) tested with a simulated engine tests/testthat/test-arreglos-dbi.R
    Oracle (fetch_first, rownum, SAMPLE) tested with a simulated engine; without a run against the real engine tests/testthat/test-dialecto-oracle.R
    BigQuery not tested —
    another engine compatible with DBI not tested; it runs through the portable path —

    The simulated engine is a subclass of the RSQLite connection. It intercepts the queries and behaves like the engine it imitates. It tests that restriction, not the engine. With another engine, another driver or another version, the function runs and declares in the coverage what it could not measure. But its figures are not checked against that engine.

    Partial failures and errors

    No block discards the other:

    • If the sample is requested and the engine rejects its query, or the sample cannot be profiled, the result comes out anyway. It carries the full resumen_tabla, perfil_muestra = NULL and a no_disponible row in the coverage, with the reason and how to solve it. If it was not requested, the row says no_solicitado, which is not a failure.
    • If the engine rejects a column, its metrics stay no_disponible and the others are profiled whole. If the read of the sample fails, the culprit column is searched for by reading the same rows with fewer columns. An alcance_distinto row names it.
    • A column that the credential cannot read, because of a per-column permission, is recognized in the catalog before reading. has_column_privilege() does it in PostgreSQL and HAS_PERMS_BY_NAME() in SQL Server. That column shows up with its metrics in no_disponible and is not named in any query.
    • With dynamic masking of SQL Server and a credential without UNMASK, completeness is published. What depends on the value stays no_disponible.
    • If a view fails on a row under muestra_motor or bloque_filas, the path tries the same summary on the whole table. The sample or the pass stay declared as no_disponible.
    • With odbc, under a locale that is not UTF-8, a column name with an accent is not sent: the column stays no_disponible. The details of encoding are in Codificación y locales (Encoding and locales, in Spanish).

    The errors of the path carry their own class, to catch them with tryCatch(). All of them inherit from lupa_error_dbi:

    • lupa_error_conexion_dbi;
    • lupa_error_tabla_dbi;
    • lupa_error_campos_dbi;
