    Dependencies and installation

    lupa has 2 required dependencies, cli and data.table. It does not import any of them into its namespace: it calls them with ::. It is deliberate: data.table decides the meaning of [ depending on whether the calling package imports it. With the import in place, tabla[, columnas, drop = FALSE] would stop selecting columns in the functions that receive a table from the user.

    data.table is used for 3 things:

    • Counting exact duplicate rows. From 25 rows, the count uses data.table::frank() with dense ranks. It falls back to duplicated() of base, which is the one that sets the result, in these cases:
      • list or compound columns;
      • NaN in double columns;
      • a duplicated() method of its own;
      • a numeric rounding setting of data.table in the session that is not exact (setNumericRounding()).
    • Copying data.table inputs before selecting columns. A table of that class is copied to a data.frame with data.table::copy(), so the [ that runs is the one of base.
    • Returning a usable data.table in remediation. aplicar() copies the input, keeps the key (setkeyv()) and restores the column reserve (setalloccol()). That way the result is still a sound data.table.

    The suggested ones are bit64, covr, DBI, duckdb, jsonlite, knitr, odbc, rJava, rmarkdown, RPostgres, RSQLite, sf, stringdist, stringi, testthat, tibble and units. In the DBI path these take part:

    • DBI;
    • the driver of each engine (RSQLite, duckdb, RPostgres, odbc);
    • bit64, which allows reading 64-bit integers in the sample without losing values.

    The drivers of other engines (RMariaDB, RMySQL, ROracle, bigrquery) are installed separately.

    The hard case is not the R package but the system library underneath. RMariaDB does not compile without the headers of the MySQL or MariaDB client, and ROracle needs the Oracle Instant Client. requisitos_motor() (engine requirements) says so before running into it.

    Its catalog has 12 entries: 9 for named engines and 3 generic ones. The 2 versions of Oracle count separately. The generic ones (dbi, odbc and otro_dbi) are not measured engines.

    r <- requisitos_motor()
knitr::kable(r[, c("id_motor", "motor", "version", "paquete_r", "dialecto",
                   "estado_prueba")], row.names = FALSE)
    id_motor motor version paquete_r dialecto estado_prueba
    dbi DBI — DBI — no_aplica
    sqlite SQLite — RSQLite limit probado
    postgresql PostgreSQL 9.3 y 16 RPostgres limit probado
    mysql MySQL 8 RMySQL limit probado
    sql_server SQL Server 2022 odbc top probado
    duckdb DuckDB 1.5 duckdb limit probado
    mariadb MariaDB 11 RMariaDB limit probado
    oracle_12c Oracle Free 23 (12c+) ROracle fetch_first esperado
    oracle_11 Oracle 11 y anteriores ROracle rownum esperado
    bigquery BigQuery — bigrquery portable no_documentado
    odbc ODBC — odbc portable no_documentado
    otro_dbi Otro compatible con DBI — — portable reserva

    Each entry also declares the system library and its package in Debian and in Fedora. If there is a way out without administrator rights, it declares it too:

    writeLines(strwrap(requisitos_motor("sql_server")$alternativa_sin_administrador, 88))
#> Compilar FreeTDS en un prefijo del usuario y pasar la ruta directa del controlador en
#> la cadena de conexión; no hace falta registrar un DSN.

    requisitos_motor() does not claim to have checked a system library that it cannot check. In that case, its status is no_comprobada (not checked).

    estado_prueba (testing status) is a declaration of the catalog, with its source in fuente_estado. esperado (expected) means that the dialect is built and tested against a simulated engine that reproduces its restriction, not against the real engine. The evidence against each engine is the run of Tested engines.

    The columns that depend on the machine —whether the R package is installed— are computed when called and are not shown here.

    Threads

    The work that can be parallelized uses 2 threads by default (getOption("lupa.nucleos", 2L)), the cap that CRAN asks to respect. It is raised per call with nucleos = 8 (cores), or for the whole session with options(lupa.nucleos = 8). The value is limited to the available cores and stays published in alcance$nucleos_usados. The result does not change, only how long it takes.

    The threads govern the text comparisons that are delegated to stringdist. They are those of:

    • detectar_duplicados_aproximados();
    • estimar_costo() (estimate cost);
    • perfilar() when approximate duplicates are requested, also for perfil_muestra through ....

    The exact count of duplicate rows uses the thread configuration of data.table itself (data.table::setDTthreads()), which the package does not change.

    Escala y duplicados (Scale and approximate duplicates, in Spanish) explains how to choose the number of threads. The times measured by number of threads, with their date and their environment, are in Evidencia y rendimiento (Evidence and performance, in Spanish).
